small_guidance:
- BLOCK_N=32 is too narrow given OC=32 — fix BLOCK_N=32 but try larger BLOCK_M (256, 512) with BLOCK_K=32/64; also add a config with num_stages=3 once SMEM allows. Verify `(BM·BK + BK·32)·4·stages ≲ 132KB`.
- The output store uses strided layout `out[b, oc, m]` (offs_n stride=OS≈122k, offs_m stride=1) — this is fine for coalescing along M, but consider writing in [N, OS, OC] (channels-last) order then permuting, so both load tiles and store tiles are contiguous along the inner BLOCK_N axis aligned with OC.
- Add a `tl.multiple_of` / `tl.max_contiguous` hint on `offs_m` and precompute `od*IHW + oh*IW + ow` once outside the K loop, so only `kd*IHW + kh*IW + kw + ic*IDHW` is added inside — reduces inner-loop index arithmetic substantially.
large_guidance:
- Switch input layout to NDHWC (channels-last) so the K-reduction axis (IC inner, then KW/KH/KD) is contiguous in memory; load a `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]` tile of the im2col patch with unit-stride gathers and a `[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N=OC]` weight tile laid out as `[IC*KD*KH*KW, OC]`. This makes `tl.dot` operate on naturally contiguous tiles and halves index math.
- Persist over the OC dimension (BLOCK_N=OC=32 fully) and tile only over (N·OS); a single program computes all 32 output channels for its M-tile, eliminating the pid_n loop and letting the weight tile be reused across the K-loop without redundant loads. Grid = (cdiv(OS, BLOCK_M), N).
- Consider a direct-conv formulation with explicit kd/kh loops (unroll KD=KH=KW=3 as constexpr) and an inner IC reduction with BLOCK_IC=8 (full IC). For IC=8, KD=KH=KW=3 the K_TOT=216 is small — a fully-unrolled 27-iter outer loop over (kd,kh,kw) with `tl.dot` on `[BLOCK_M, IC] × [IC, OC]` per kernel position avoids the modular-arithmetic decoding inside the K-loop entirely.
